SparkR / SPARKR-145
Develop a serializer&deserializer for R objects in JVM
Issue Type: New Feature
Assignee: Unassigned
Created: 11/Dec/14 1:03 AM
Priority: Major
Reporter: Sun Rui

Develop a serializer&deserializer which can serialize Java objects to R objects and deserialize Java objects from R objects (Something like the Java pickler&unpickler used by PySpark). This feature provides the foundation for further developments, such as MLLib integration, read from and save as Hadoop files whose content is in Java data types that can be recognized by JVM languages, etc.

In the short term, May use JRI of the R rjava package for this purpose. However, JRI internally loads an R engine as the agent instead of direct serialization and deserialization, which may suffer performance penalty.

In the long term, the serde may be implemented by directly parsing/generating R objects.

list, numeric, character, integer could be supported first.

Re: Develop a serializer&deserializer for R objects in JVM

Thanks Sun Rui for opening this issue. I think this is a good idea and something that will be useful across multiple efforts at integration (MLLib, SparkSQL, ML Pipelines etc.) In fact I would actually suggest addressing this issue first instead of using JRI (that adds another dependency which I'd like to avoid if possible).

Note that we already have some routines which we use to communicate between Java and R in serialize.R Right now, this includes functions to read, write integers and strings (on the Java side we just use DataInputStream/DataOutputStream in RRDD.scala )

The next steps I see for this JIRA are:
1. Pull out the serialize, deserialize functions we have into a separate module.
2. Implement serializers, deserializers for numeric (doubles) and arrays of primitive types.

Re: Develop a serializer&deserializer for R objects in JVM

Thanks Antonio Piccolboni for taking a look. The serializers, deserializers are right now only used in the R to Java bridge which is the control path and not the data path. i.e. These are mostly used to send high-level messages like 'createSparkContext' or 'call rdd.cache' etc. Also in this case we want to serialize, deserialize native Java types (those are the arguments to the functions) and it'll be tricky to wrap every native types in a protobuf message.

For the data path, we are still using R's serialization (i.e. just calling `serialize`) and I do remember that we discussed the performance penalties in using that before. We have a different challenge there as it needs to work with arbitrary types in R. I think we will see some of these performance penalties during the SparkSQL integration and my hope is we can then figure out what parts need to be in C vs R etc.

Re: Develop a serializer&deserializer for R objects in JVM

Thanks Antonio Piccolboni for the pointers to other packages. I think there is a technical question here and a licensing question and we need to look at them separately

  • The first is the technical question what is the most efficient serialization format for SparkR's requirements. As I said before, for the control path using hand-wrapped serialization is fast enough (our RPCs to the SparkRBackend take ~1 millisecond or so right now). For the data path we have been using R's native serialization partly because it is general and partly because it is the first thing we got working. We haven't had the chance to try out other techniques or do a thorough performance comparison and we welcome any efforts in this direction. There are some efforts in the community like the upcoming Spark Summit talk [1] on using Renjin and keeping everything in the JVM which are very promising.
  • On the licensing side thanks for the pointers to packages like Histogramtools, foreach. Given that the way the project is growing, we are hopeful of merging SparkR with the Apache Spark project at some point. In that case, the ASF legal team might also be able to provide more guidance on how to interpret licenses for R package dependencies. That said I'd like to keep this JIRA for discussing the technical aspects of serialization, deserialization first and discuss the licensing issue when we have a particular PR up for consideration.

[1] http://spark-summit.org/east/2015/talk/functionality-and-performance-improvement-of-sparkr-and-its-application
